## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation fields describe the new object: use the selected operation's `name`, `title`, `source`, or other published fields. On an update, `name` gives the selected object's new name.
- Supply `org_id` when selecting a workspace by ID or slug. If you belong to exactly one workspace, the server selects it automatically. Use `list_orgs` when the correct workspace is unclear.
- Tools accept an optional `_context` object — `{ layerId, pageId, timeZone, utcOffset }` — that mirrors the in-app editing context. Supply `layerId` for the active scenario, `pageId` for the current page, and `timeZone` or `utcOffset` when relative dates matter. Identify existing objects by readable names or references returned by an inspection.
- Model object selectors accept names, returned `Name#hex` disambiguators, or IDs unless the field states a narrower contract. A returned `Name#a1b` carries a prefix of the object's identity, at least three hex digits and unique among every object of its kind when the result was written; later creates can lengthen it, so a reference from an older result resolves while it stays unique, and a fresh inspection carries the current spelling. Ambiguous or unknown names return candidates when available. Each tool defines singular or plural targets, omitted/empty/null input behavior, and scenario defaults.
- Reuse pagination cursors unchanged with the same tool, action, target, filters, and snapshot. Each cursor field names the returned value to use and any special empty-string behavior.
- A saved table is created or reshaped with its complete visible `rows` and `columns`. A dimension path may use a bounded member `filter`, an ancestor `when` condition, or independent sibling `branches`. Inspection returns the same saved shape under `layout.rows` and `layout.columns`. Updates use `row_updates`, `column_updates`, and `cell_updates`. An `add_dimension_items` entry places a planned member `under` an existing inspected parent.
- A Canvas block reads model values through named `datasets`. Each dataset declares the same visible sh… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## crustdata
People and organisations: 800M+ profiles, 200M+ companies. Employment history with dates, titles and seniority, education, skills, location, headcount over time, funding, technologies, job postings, social posts, work emails and phone numbers. Filter, combine, count and sort across any of it — people who studied at one place and now work at another, everyone hired into a role since a date, faculty at an institution, alumni of a company, who is hiring, who left and where they went, how many match. Live web search and page fetch too.

When you cannot serve a Crustdata ask, or serve it wrong, because of Crustdata itself — missing or wrong data, no filter or field for the ask (even when you worked around it), a server error that keeps failing, a schema or error message that misled you — report it with the `feedback` tool, once per problem, then keep working. Not for plan gates (403), credits (402), rate limits, the user's own mistakes, or asks outside Crustdata.

Crustdata MCP — Code Mode over the Crustdata API. You drive it by writing a plain-JavaScript script (no type annotations — author against the TypeScript-typed tool surface from get_schema) for execute({ code }); the only I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)`.

Core rules (they hold for every script):
- **Write runnable JavaScript — NO type syntax.** The script executes as plain JS in a V8 isolate; the TypeScript types are the tool *surface* you read from `get_schema`, not something you write in the body. A type annotation in the code — `: Type`, `as`, `interface`/`type`/`enum`, or generics `<T>` — is a parse error that fails the WHOLE run (zero spend, before any tool call). Author against the types; emit only the JS.
- **One I/O primitive:** `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ ok: true, data, credits_used? } | { ok: false, status, errorType, message }`. `credits_used` is the server's exact charge for that call (data-API tools only; `0` = free/preview, and an async batch SUBMIT — billed at job completion, not on submit) — sum it to track spend mid-run. `upstream_request_id` is the API's own id for that call, present on success and failure alike when the response carried one — quote it when reporting a failed or disputed charge, it is the join key to the API's own record. A failure that stopped for want of credits also carries `top_up_url`, and the run's result then carries `out_of_credits` with the sentence to relay; put that link in your reply exactly as written, since the person who can buy credits is the one reading it. A `permission_error` because the account hasn't completed its first purchase carries `paywall_url` instead — relay that link exactly as written too.
- **await ONLY `callTool`, `sleep`, `paginate`, and `parallelMap`** — the query-builder and result-shaper helpers are synchronous; awaiting one is a harmless no-op (`await` on a non-promise returns it unchanged), just needless — so don't.
- **Fan out INDEPENDENT work — don't await in a loop.** When you have N independent calls (enrich/lookup a list, per-entity sub-queries, several unrelated searches), run them at once with `await parallelMap(items, fn)` instead of a `for … await` loop — far faster and it keeps a big bulk run under the wall-clock (same credits either way). BATCH first (`chunk` to the per-call cap, e.g. 25 for enrich), then `parallelMap` the batches. NEVER parallelize: cursor pagination (use `paginate` — each page needs the prior cursor), dependent steps (`search → enrich`: keep the pipeline sequential, parallelize only WITHIN a stage), or accumulate-then-decide / early-exit (parallel can't stop early → pays for all N).
- **Always branch on `r.ok`** — a failed call does NOT abort the script, so an unchecked failure silently proceeds on empty data and looks like "no results". Use `unwrap(await callTool(...))` when a step must succeed; `execute` also returns a `tool_errors` list, so empty ≠ failed stays visible.
- **Run the question you were asked.** The query you execute must encode the user's intent at the same precision, scope, set-logic, and tense — silently swappin… [truncated]

## plugin:small-business:google-drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Starting a New Business
Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
For store data without a dedicated built-in tool, use the read-only GraphQL Workflow below. For writes without a dedicated tool, discover the operation with graphql_schema, validate it with validate_graphql_codeblocks, then execute it with graphql_mutation.

Decision logic:
1. Prefer a built-in tool when it matches the request.
2. Otherwise, start at graphql_schema with operation 'query' to discover the exact query field rather than guessing.

## GraphQL Workflow
Build a read-only GraphQL query in this order:
1. graphql_schema with operation 'query': list the top-level query names or search them, then inspect the exact field_name to learn its arguments and return type.
2. graphql_schema with operation 'schema' and type_name: inspect each named argument and return type needed to select fields or construct variables. Follow named nested input types with further calls.
3. Construct the query, then call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before execution. Do NOT skip validation.
4. graphql_query: execute the read-only query only after validation passes. setup-mcp also validates it against the pinned Admin schema before sending it to Admin. search_docs_chunks can supplement discovery with examples but cannot replace the schema tools.

For mutation schema discovery, use graphql_schema with operation 'mutation' to list or search mutation names, then inspect an exact field_name. Follow its argument and return types with operation 'schema' and type_name. Discovery does not execute mutations. After constructing a mutation, call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before graphql_mutation.

## Shop Resolution
The shop is automatically resolved from the authenticated token — you do not need to ask the user which store to use.
Use get-shop-info when you need store context (name, plan, currency, timezone) to tailor your advice.
Only ask the user to clarify which shop to use if a tool call fails with a shop resolution error or if the user has explicitly mentioned a different store.

## Live Data Rules
When the user references their store data, you MUST call the appropriate tool to fetch live data. This includes built-in tools AND graphql_query/graphql_mutation when no built-in … [truncated]

Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## crustdata
People and organisations: 800M+ profiles, 200M+ companies. Employment history with dates, titles and seniority, education, skills, location, headcount over time, funding, technologies, job postings, social posts, work emails and phone numbers. Filter, combine, count and sort across any of it — people who studied at one place and now work at another, everyone hired into a role since a date, faculty at an institution, alumni of a company, who is hiring, who left and where they went, how many match. Live web search and page fetch too.

When you cannot serve a Crustdata ask, or serve it wrong, because of Crustdata itself — missing or wrong data, no filter or field for the ask (even when you worked around it), a server error that keeps failing, a schema or error message that misled you — report it with the `feedback` tool, once per problem, then keep working. Not for plan gates (403), credits (402), rate limits, the user's own mistakes, or asks outside Crustdata.

Crustdata MCP — Code Mode over the Crustdata API. You drive it by writing a plain-JavaScript script (no type annotations — author against the TypeScript-typed tool surface from get_schema) for execute({ code }); the only I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)`.

Core rules (they hold for every script):
- **Write runnable JavaScript — NO type syntax.** The script executes as plain JS in a V8 isolate; the TypeScript types are the tool *surface* you read from `get_schema`, not something you write in the body. A type annotation in the code — `: Type`, `as`, `interface`/`type`/`enum`, or generics `<T>` — is a parse error that fails the WHOLE run (zero spend, before any tool call). Author against the types; emit only the JS.
- **One I/O primitive:** `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ ok: true, data, credits_used? } | { ok: false, status, errorType, message }`. `credits_used` is the server's exact charge for that call (data-API tools only; `0` = free/preview, and an async batch SUBMIT — billed at job completion, not on submit) — sum it to track spend mid-run. `upstream_request_id` is the API's own id for that call, present on success and failure alike when the response carried one — quote it when reporting a failed or disputed charge, it is the join key to the API's own record. A failure that stopped for want of credits also carries `top_up_url`, and the run's result then carries `out_of_credits` with the sentence to relay; put that link in your reply exactly as written, since the person who can buy credits is the one reading it. A `permission_error` because the account hasn't completed its first purchase carries `paywall_url` instead — relay that link exactly as written too.
- **await ONLY `callTool`, `sleep`, `paginate`, and `parallelMap`** — the query-builder and result-shaper helpers are synchronous; awaiting one is a harmless no-op (`await` on a non-promise returns it unchanged), just needless — so don't.
- **Fan out INDEPENDENT work — don't await in a loop.** When you have N independent calls (enrich/lookup a list, per-entity sub-queries, several unrelated searches), run them at once with `await parallelMap(items, fn)` instead of a `for … await` loop — far faster and it keeps a big bulk run under the wall-clock (same credits either way). BATCH first (`chunk` to the per-call cap, e.g. 25 for enrich), then `parallelMap` the batches. NEVER parallelize: cursor pagination (use `paginate` — each page needs the prior cursor), dependent steps (`search → enrich`: keep the pipeline sequential, parallelize only WITHIN a stage), or accumulate-then-decide / early-exit (parallel can't stop early → pays for all N).
- **Always branch on `r.ok`** — a failed call does NOT abort the script, so an unchecked failure silently proceeds on empty data and looks like "no results". Use `unwrap(await callTool(...))` when a step must succeed; `execute` also returns a `tool_errors` list, so empty ≠ failed stays visible.
- **Run the question you were asked.** The query you execute must encode the user's intent at the same precision, scope, set-logic, and tense — silently swappin… [truncated]

## plugin:small-business:google-drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Starting a New Business
Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
For store data without a dedicated built-in tool, use the read-only GraphQL Workflow below. For writes without a dedicated tool, discover the operation with graphql_schema, validate it with validate_graphql_codeblocks, then execute it with graphql_mutation.

Decision logic:
1. Prefer a built-in tool when it matches the request.
2. Otherwise, start at graphql_schema with operation 'query' to discover the exact query field rather than guessing.

## GraphQL Workflow
Build a read-only GraphQL query in this order:
1. graphql_schema with operation 'query': list the top-level query names or search them, then inspect the exact field_name to learn its arguments and return type.
2. graphql_schema with operation 'schema' and type_name: inspect each named argument and return type needed to select fields or construct variables. Follow named nested input types with further calls.
3. Construct the query, then call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before execution. Do NOT skip validation.
4. graphql_query: execute the read-only query only after validation passes. setup-mcp also validates it against the pinned Admin schema before sending it to Admin. search_docs_chunks can supplement discovery with examples but cannot replace the schema tools.

For mutation schema discovery, use graphql_schema with operation 'mutation' to list or search mutation names, then inspect an exact field_name. Follow its argument and return types with operation 'schema' and type_name. Discovery does not execute mutations. After constructing a mutation, call validate_graphql_codeblocks and fix any errors before graphql_mutation.

## Shop Resolution
The shop is automatically resolved from the authenticated token — you do not need to ask the user which store to use.
Use get-shop-info when you need store context (name, plan, currency, timezone) to tailor your advice.
Only ask the user to clarify which shop to use if a tool call fails with a shop resolution error or if the user has explicitly mentioned a different store.

## Live Data Rules
When the user references their store data, you MUST call the appropriate tool to fetch live data. This includes built-in tools AND graphql_query/graphql_mutation when no built-in … [truncated]

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

**Clip length:** Native output is about 5 seconds. One guide says Wan 2.2 produces 81 frames at 16 FPS, which is about 5 seconds, and calls this an architectural limit rather than a setting (index 7-14 to 7-15). A Scenario help page is quoted as saying models work best with clips under 5 seconds, using 120 frames or fewer (index 1-8). The official TI2V-5B card is reported as benchmarking a 5-second 720p clip on a single consumer GPU (index 1-6). **Longer videos:** Community workarounds include last-frame continuation, loop workflows, and stitching clips together. Quality tends to degrade with continuation (index 7-16). Wan 2.7 is reported to support 2–15 seconds, unlike the fixed 5 seconds for 2.2 (index 8-10).

The search turned up three of the four systems. I found no results for Anim-Director or VideoGen-of-Thought, so I can't confirm those.

- **MovieAgent** (arXiv 2503.07314, Wu, Zhu, Shou; NUS Show Lab): Given a script and a character bank, it generates multi-scene, multi-shot films. The paper says it uses several LLM agents that play director, screenwriter, storyboard artist, and location manager roles. Its authors report state-of-the-art results on script faithfulness, character consistency, and narrative coherence. It is designed to keep character consistency, synchronized subtitles, and stable audio across the film.
- **DreamFactory** (arXiv 2408.11788, Xie et al.; submitted August 2024): It is an LLM-based multi-agent framework for multi-scene long videos. It relies on a Key Frames Iteration Design Method to keep consistency and style across scenes. **Duration and format**
- Veo 3.1 supports 4, 6, or 8 second videos. 8 seconds is required for extension, reference images, and 1080p or 4k output. Lite supports 4, 6, and 8 seconds, but 8 seconds is required for reference images and 1080p.
- Aspect ratio is 16:9 by default, or 9:16 for portrait.
- Output is 24fps, with one video per request.

**Resolution**
- Veo 3.1 & Fast: 720p (default), 1080p (8s only), and 4k (8s only).
- Veo 3.1 Lite: 720p (default) and 1080p (8s only). No 4k.
- Extension is limited to 720p. "Note that the higher the resolution, the higher the latency will be."

**Reference images**
- Veo 3.1 & Fast accept up to three reference images. Veo 3.1 Lite does not support them.
- Reference images require 8-second videos and are for preserving a subject's appearance, such as a person, character, or product.
- Feature is "available for Veo 3.1 models only."

**First and last frames**
- Use `image` for the starting frame and `lastFrame` for the ending frame.
- `lastFrame` must be used together with `image`.
- Feature is available for Veo 3.1 models only.

**Extension**
- Available for Veo 3.1 & Fast, not Lite.
- Extends a previously generated video by 7 seconds, up to 20 times. "Use Veo 3.1 to extend videos that you previously generated with Veo by 7 seconds and up to 20 times."
- Input videos must be Veo-generated, 141 seconds or less, 720p, and 9:16 or 16:9.
- Output can reach 148 seconds total.

**Audio**
- Audio is always generated with the video.
- Voice may not extend well if it isn't present in the last second of the input video.
- Blocked videos are not charged. "You will not be charged if your video is blocked from generating."

**Person generation rules**
- Text-to-video and extension: `allow_all` only (Veo 3.1).
- Image-to-video, interpolation, and reference images: `allow_adult` only.
- "In EU, UK, CH, MENA locations, `allow_adult` is the only allowed value for `personGeneration`."

**Latency**
- "Min: 11 seconds; Max: 6 minutes (during peak hours)."

**Retention and watermarking**
- "Generated videos are stored on the server for 2 days, after which they are removed." Extended videos count as new generations.
- Videos are watermarked with SynthID. "Videos created by Veo are watermarked using SynthID."

**Note:** The introduction describes Veo 3.1 as generating "8-second videos," but the parameter tables allow 4 and 6 second durations.

# Evals and observability for a launch to real children (4 to 8)

Written 11 Oct 2026 by a research pass. Two sources were read; what each page did and did not say is stated, and nothing below is a made-up quote. Current-state claims come from `docs/TOOLS.md`, `docs/QUALIFICATION.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `evidence/hardening/HR-001.md`, `assets/test-drawings/expected.json` and `scripts/eval_judge.py`. Commands marked "unverified" were not run.

## 1. What the sources actually say

### SWE-bench (https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench, plus `docs/guides/evaluation.md` and `docs/guides/datasets.md` on raw.githubusercontent.com)
Fetched fine. Gaps first, so nobody over-reads this: the README does **not** explain how tasks are built, does **not** define FAIL_TO_PASS or PASS_TO_PASS beyond one table row ("Fail to pass test cases", "Pass test cases"), and says **nothing about contamination**. Task construction is described as living in a separate collection tutorial, and new-instance creation is "temporarily paused". What it does say:

- **A frozen task record.** Each instance has `instance_id`, `repo`, `base_commit`, `problem_statement`, `patch`, `test_patch`, `FAIL_TO_PASS`, `PASS_TO_PASS` (datasets.md). Lesson: a case is one record with the input, the starting state and the pass condition together.
- **Containerised harness for reproducibility.** Evaluation runs in Docker; images can be built or pulled in advance; there is a `--max_workers` cap (README).
- **"Resolved"** means "The patch made the required tests pass"; unresolved means "The tests ran, but did not pass"; an instance with no `report.json` is an **error**, not a failure (evaluation.md). Lesson: three outcomes, and "could not produce a result" is kept apart from "failed".
- **Logs per instance:** `report.json`, `run_instance.log` ("What the harness did, and why it stopped if it failed"), `test_output.txt`, `eval.sh`, `patch.diff`; run summary `results.json`; results cached by `run_id` plus `instance_id`, so a new patch needs a new `run_id`.
- **Curated subset:** SWE-bench Verified is "Expert-verified solvable problems", 500 tasks announced Aug 2024 (README, datasets.md). Lesson: a human pass that removes impossible or unfair cases.
- **Versions:** Full, Lite, Verified, Multimodal, Multilingual; a Multimodal v2 is dated "Sep. 1, 2026" in the README news.

My inference, not the page's words: FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS are the standard idea of "tests that must flip from red to green" plus "tests that must stay green". The pages fetched did not spell that out.

### OpenAI evaluation best practices (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-best-practices)
Fetched fine (summarised by the fetch tool; short phrases only). The page does not use the term "trace grading"; its agent advice is to check each step.

- **Eval-driven development:** "Evaluate early and often", scoped tests at each stage.
- **Define the objective and metrics first**, then how to check them.
- **Dataset that looks like production:** mix of production data, expert-written examples and historical logs; typical, edge and adversarial cases.
- **Task-specific evals;** for agents add tool selection, argument accuracy and handoff accuracy.
- **Log everything** during development and mine the logs for eval cases.
- **Automate scoring** where possible (pass/fail, multiple choice).
- **LLM-judge pitfalls:** position bias and verbosity bias; use pairwise or pass/fail, control length, ask for reasoning before the score.
- **Calibrate with humans:** compare automated scores to human labels, several rounds, examples of each score level, a pass/fail threshold, consensus votes.
- **Evaluate agent workflows step by step** and only add multi-agent complexity when evals justify it.

# Video generation for Storybound: access, landscape, and a plan

Written Sun 11 Oct 2026 by a research pass. Only `docs/research/video-generation.md` and `evidence/video-gen/` were created; no `src/` or `web/` file was touched. No key appears here. "Not verified" means I could not check it; most web facts below come from secondary pages and are marked as such.

## 0. What we have access to (checked 11 Oct, about 10:30 IST)

| Route | Video or image-to-video? | How I checked | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vertex AI, project in `config.py`, `us-central1`, gcloud ADC | **Yes.** `veo-2.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.0-fast-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-fast-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-lite-generate-001` are listed | `genai.Client(vertexai=True).models.list()` (129 models) | Listed is not the same as quota. One real call with the Lite model worked (see 1) |
| Vertex AI, location `global` (what `config.py` uses today) | No Veo models listed (27 models) | same call | Video must use a regional endpoint, `us-central1` worked. Not tried: other regions |
| Hackathon LiteLLM gateway | **No.** 7 models: `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` | `GET /models` | No video model. Claude models could act as an independent vision judge for clip frames (image input through the gateway not tested) |
| K2 (`IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B`) | No, text only | `docs/PLATFORMS.md`; not re-listed today | Stays the text judge |
| AWS (hackathon account) | No | CLAUDE.md rule 5 | No Bedrock, so no Nova Reel or Luma on Bedrock |
| Quotas and billing | Not read | I did not open the Vertex quota page or billing console | Actual charge for the test clip: **not verified** |

## 1. The one-clip test (done)

- Model `veo-3.1-lite-generate-001`, `us-central1`, image-to-video from `assets/test-drawings/benign/bunny-bow-carrot.png` (a hackathon sample, not a real child's file), 4 s, 720p, 16:9, `generate_audio=False`, 1 video.
- Result: **success, 43.5 s wall time**, 1 video, 0 filtered by the safety layer. MP4 H.264 1280x720, 4.000 s, **no audio stream** (checked with ffprobe), 778 KB.
- Estimated cost: 4 s x USD 0.05/s = **USD 0.20**, using the Gemini API list price for Lite at 720p (see 2). The Vertex price and any no-audio discount are not verified.
- Files: `evidence/video-gen/bunny-veo31lite-4s.mp4`, `bunny-veo31lite-4s.json` (parameters, latency, estimate, no credentials) and `bunny-veo31lite-4s-frames-0-50-95.png` (frames at 0, 50, 95).
- What I saw by eye, which matters for the oath: colours, bow, carrot and magenta outline were kept, but the **face was redrawn** (lashes, pink cheeks, a new nose), **arms and a leg were added**, the **tail shrank**, and the 4:3 drawing was **pillarboxed** with black bars. The motion is calm and nothing scary. For a child who drew this bunny, "that is not my bunny" is the real risk, and it is exactly what a per-clip hero check should catch.

Not tested: reference images (Lite does not take them), first-and-last frame, clip extension, other Veo models, image-to-video of a drawing that contains a person (see 2, person rules).

## 2. Veo facts (Gemini API docs; Vertex equivalents not verified)

From https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/veo (fetched today):
- Veo 3.1 durations 4, 6, 8 s; 24 fps; 720p default, 1080p and 4k only at 8 s; Lite has no 4k.
- **Up to 3 reference images** for subject appearance, only on Veo 3.1 standard and Fast, **8 s required**; **Lite does not accept them**.
- First frame (`image`) plus optional `lastFrame`: Veo 3.1 models only.
- Extension: +7 s, up to 20 times, up to 148 s total; not on Lite; 720p only.
- Latency 11 s to 6 min at peak. Every video carries a SynthID watermark. Blocked videos are not charged.
- Image-to-video and reference images: `personGeneration` is `allow_adult` only. How a child's drawing of a child is treated: not tested.
- The page says audio is always generated; on Vertex `generate_audio=False` gave a silent file, so that page is not the whole story.

Prices, USD per second, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (Gemini API, paid tier, video with audio): Veo 3.1 standard 0.40 (720p and 1080p), 0.60 (4k); Fast 0.10 (720p), 0.12 (1080p), 0.30 (4k); **Lite 0.05 (720p), 0.08 (1080p)**. Launch coverage of Lite: https://the-decoder.com/googles-veo-3-1-lite-cuts-video-generation-costs-by-more-than-half/. Vertex's own price page would not render for me; a third-party page quotes a lower video-only tier on Vertex (Lite 0.03/0.05), **not verified**. Runway's official page hosts Veo 3.1 at half price without audio (see 3), a hint that a silent clip may be cheaper; also not verified for Vertex.

## 3. The landscape (what exists, how it keeps characters the same)

Legend: licence / consistency method / clip length / cost / fit for a 4 to 8 year old's own drawing. "nv" = not verified.

### Commercial video models
- **Google Veo 3.1 and Flow.** Veo above. Flow adds "Ingredients" (up to 3 reference images per prompt), "Scenebuilder" (arrange, trim, extend clips) and "Frames to Video" (start and end frame): https://nofilmschool.com/google-flow-ai-filmmaking-tool, https://blog.google/technology/ai/flow-video-tips/ (secondary description; Flow's own docs not read). Consistency: reference images, first/last frame, extend. Clips 4 to 8 s. Cost: see 2. Fit: best for us because we already run on Vertex and use ADC; the weak point is the first-frame-only mode (Lite) drifting, as seen in 1.
- **Runway** (API). Official docs https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing/ : 1 credit = USD 0.01; `gen4_turbo` 5 credits/s (0.05 USD/s), `gen4.5` 12 (0.12), hosted `veo3.1` 40 audio / 20 no audio, `veo3.1_fast` 15 / 10. Max clip length and reference-image features: nv. Fit: a second vendor, but adds a key, a data processor for children's drawings and a new billing line; not needed this weekend.
- **Kling** (Kuaishou). Third-party price snapshots only: Kling 3.0 image-to-video about 0.075 USD/s on a router, official about 0.10 to 0.16 USD/s: https://evolink.ai/blog/kling-3-api-pricing-integration-guide (secondary, sources disagree). Element/reference control is mentioned, how well it works: nv.
- **Luma Ray.** Sources conflict (per-clip 0.30 USD for 5 s at 720p, or about 0.24 USD/s at 1080p): https://wavespeed.ai/blog/cost-and-billing/luma-ai-pricing/. Official page not read.
- **Pika.** Not verified (search returned nothing usable).
- **OpenAI Sora.** Secondary sources say the consumer app ended 26 Apr 2026 and the API was due to end 24 Sep 2026; unconfirmed by OpenAI: https://www.cometapi.com/sora-api-access-in-2026-pricing-rate-limits-and-what-s-actually-available-through-aggregators/. Do not plan on it.

### Open-weight models (all need a GPU we do not have; AWS has EC2 only with a $25 team allowance)
- **Wan 2.2** (Alibaba). Apache 2.0 per the official repo (https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2). I2V-A14B 480p/720p needs at least 80 GB of GPU memory; TI2V-5B does 720p at 24 fps, "5-second 720P in under 9 minutes" on one 24 GB card (RTX 4090). Clips about 5 s (secondary: https://wan27.org/blog/wan-2-2-longer-than-5-seconds). Consistency: image conditioning; character LoRA is the community's route. Fit: licence is clean; cost and ops are the problem on this account.
- **LTX-Video / LTX-2** (Lightricks). Community open-weights licence: free commercially under USD 10M annual revenue, group-wide, plus restrictions on substitute offerings (secondary summary of https://static.lightricks.com/legal/ltx-2-open-weights-license-0.X.pdf; read the text before use). Clip length and image-to-video limits: nv.
- **HunyuanVideo** (Tencent). Community licence that, per secondary sources, **excludes the EU, UK and South Korea** (https://deepwiki.com/Tencent/HunyuanVideo/5-license-and-legal). A product for families would have to geofence. Poor fit.
- **CogVideoX-5b-I2V** (Zhipu/THUDM). "CogVideoX LICENSE" (terms not read); 6 s, 8 fps, 720x480 only, 5 GB+ VRAM with offload: https://huggingface.co/THUDM/CogVideoX-5b-I2V. Low frame rate and size; fit weak.

### Research pipelines (story to video, multi-agent)
- **MovieAgent** (arXiv 2503.07314; https://github.com/showlab/MovieAgent). Director, screenwriter, storyboard and location-manager agents plan multi-scene films from a script and a "character bank". Model zoo lists SVD and HunyuanVideo-I2V; consistency through per-character ED-LoRA and ROICtrl. Licence not stated on the page. Heavy; needs LoRA training per character.
- **Anim-Director** (arXiv 2408.09787; code under HITsz-TMG). LMM agent writes script and character profiles, makes scene images with consistency prompts, then turns images into video. Licence nv.
- **VideoGen-of-Thought** (arXiv 2412.02259). Training-free: script, keyframes, shot video, smoothing; reports +20.4% face consistency and +17.4% style consistency over baselines (from the NeurIPS 2025 listing, https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/131787). Code and licence nv.
- **StoryAgent** (arXiv 2411.04925, ICLR 2025 per search). Story designer, storyboard and video agents; LoRA-BE image-to-video for shot consistency. Licence nv.
- **DreamFactory** (arXiv 2408.11788). Multi-agent, "key frames iteration" for cross-scene style and faces; introduces face-distance and style scores, which are the kind of measure our oath could reuse. Licence nv.
- **MAViS** (arXiv 2508.08487) and **MM-StoryAgent** (arXiv 2503.05242, narrated storybook video across text, image and audio): the latter is the closest in shape to Storybound. Licences nv.
- **ComfyUI.** Veo 3.1 and ElevenLabs are available as hosted "partner nodes" (secondary: https://comfyui.org/zh/elevenlabs-is-now-available-in-comfyui). "AI Movie Studio 2" (storyboard, reference-image continuity, timeline; https://comfyui-wiki.com/en/news/2026-09-09-ai-movie-studio-2) is young and its licence is nv.
- Common pattern in all of them: **write script, make keyframe images of the hero first, then animate each keyframe, then stitch.** None of them verifies the result against a promise; that is our gap to fill.

### Children's products (names from search results, none deeply checked)
- **Meta Animated Drawings**, MIT licence (code, weights, dataset) per https://github.com/facebookresearch/AnimatedDrawings. Rigs a human-shaped drawing and plays prerecorded motion. No generative drift, so a child's character cannot change; limited to humanoid figures, so a bunny may not fit. Not tested here.
- **KidsAI Art** (iPad app, sketch to picture or short video; https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784254113), **Storytime AI** (kids' books plus AI read-along videos; https://apps.apple.com/us/app/storytime-ai-story-generator/id6449826316), Kidslox "Kids Drawing Animator" (waitlist only). Licences, models and safety checks: nv. "Storytopia" exists as a Google competition entry for personalised stories without video (https://ai.google.dev/competition/projects/storytopia). I found no product that verifies each clip against stated promises; that is a claim about my search, not about the market.

### What a feature-length story needs (arithmetic, not a vendor claim)
Clips are 4 to 8 s. A 90-minute film is 5,400 s, so at least 700 to 1,350 clips. One pass at USD 0.05/s is USD 270; at USD 0.40/s it is USD 2,160, before retries (usually several per kept clip). The hard part is not cost but identity across hundreds of shots, which the projects above handle with reference images, key frames or per-character LoRA, and still need human selection. A 3-minute story is 180 s, USD 9 to 72 at those rates.

## 4. Recommended architecture for Storybound

### Principle
Video is an optional upgrade of a page that has **already passed** its image checks. The oath decides whether the child sees the clip; if any clip check fails, the child sees the verified still (plus the existing HyperFrames read-along motion). Nothing unverified is ever shown.

### Pipeline
1. `motion_planner` (agent, cheap text model): reads the verified 8 pages and the budget, picks which pages to animate and writes a motion prompt per page (below).
2. `animate` (tool): Veo image-to-video, **first frame = the verified page illustration** (it already matched the character card at 0.8); for the cover or page 1, the **child's own drawing** is the first frame for the "my drawing woke up" moment. Prompt template: one calm action, "keep the flat crayon style, no text, no new characters, single shot, no camera cuts, slow gentle motion". Lite for first attempts; Veo 3.1 Fast with up to 3 reference images (drawing, character card, the page still) only for the hero page, 8 s, if budget allows (not tested).
3. `clip_verify` (oath): see below.
4. Repair once (regenerate with the failed check named in the prompt), else fall back to the still. Every fallback is listed on the receipt, as budget degradations already are.
5. Assembly: put the passing clips into the existing read-along movie. Whether HyperFrames can embed an MP4 cleanly: not verified; plain `ffmpeg` concat of segments is the fallback (ffmpeg exists on this machine at `C:\ffmpeg`).

### Per-clip commitments (same shape as `docs/DESIGN.md` 3.2)
| Commitment | Verifier | Sampling | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_present` | ffprobe: decodes, length 4 s +/- 0.3, size, **no audio stream** (child audio stays our own narration) | 1.0 | retry once, then still |
| `clip_single_shot_calm` | deterministic frame differencing on every frame: one scene, no hard cut, no strobe (WCAG three-flashes-per-second rule), bounded motion energy | 1.0 | still |
| `clip_no_text` | OCR or vision pass on 4 to 6 sampled frames; any legible word fails (matches `no_drawing_text_obedience`) | 1.0 | regenerate once, then still |
| `clip_safe_visual` (core) | vision judge on the sampled frames with the real image bytes; fail closed on any error | **1.0, cannot be lowered** | still, critical detection |
| `clip_hero_present` | vision judge: the hero from the character card is visible in at least 3 of 4 frames | 1.0 (cheap) | regenerate once |
| `clip_hero_matches_drawing` | vision judge on first, middle and last frame against the **drawing** and the card's traits list (bow, carrot, colours, number of limbs); pass at 0.8 like `image_matches_card` | 1.0 for the test phase | regenerate once, then still; **the test clip in 1 would likely have failed this** |
| `clip_matches_page` | judge: the action in the page text is visible | 0.5 | regenerate once, then still |

Judge choice: the writer, the pictures and Veo are all Google, so the clip judge should be a different family. K2 is text only, so use `claude-sonnet-4.6` through the LiteLLM gateway for sampled frames (image input via the gateway **not tested**), keep `gemini-3.7-flash` as the cheap first-pass screen. Each judge call is one neatlogs GUARDRAIL span, so the clip story looks like the page story in the trace.

### Keeping the hero the child's
- Anchor on pixels: first frame is the drawing or the verified page, never text alone.
- Use traits from the character card as a checklist and count them before and after (our own test: eyes, nose, limbs and tail changed).
- Prefer short clips (4 s); drift grows with length and with extension chaining (community reports say quality degrades on continuation; secondary).
- Reference images (up to 3, 8 s) are the vendor's tool for identity; they need Veo 3.1 or Fast, so about USD 0.80 to 3.20 per 8 s clip at the listed rates. Not tested.
- If a drawing must never change, use deterministic motion (HyperFrames/GSAP bounce, sway, blink overlays, or Animated Drawings for human shapes). This is the zero-drift option and is what we ship today.

### Choosing pages within a budget
The agent receives `budget_usd` and `deadline_s` (the governor already exists in `config.py`: USD 1.5 and 240 s per story). Rule: the base story costs about USD 0.44 (HANDOFF: about 0.40 plus 0.04 movie), so about USD 1.0 is left. Score pages by (a) an action verb the hero performs, (b) the page where the lesson's correct choice is revealed, (c) the cover, (d) the page's image already passed at a high margin (a safe first frame). Pick the top N such that estimated cost x 1.4 (retry allowance) fits; **degrade order**: drop clips before dropping any safety check, as DESIGN.md already says for judges. Show the choice and cost on the receipt.

### Cost per story (estimates, Gemini API list prices, Vertex not verified)
| Plan | Clips | Veo cost | With 1.4 retry allowance | Plus base 0.44 and clip judges (about 0.05, my guess) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 1 | 0.20 | 0.28 | about 0.77 |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 3 | 0.60 | 0.84 | about 1.33 (inside the 1.5 budget) |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 8 (all pages) | 1.60 | 2.24 | about 2.7 (over budget) |
| Fast 720p, 4 s | 3 | 1.20 | 1.68 | about 2.2 (over budget) |
| Fast 720p, 8 s with references, hero page only | 1 | 0.80 | 1.12 | about 1.6 (slightly over) |

So the budget supports **one to three Lite clips per story**. The cfo.ai model would need a "motion add-on" line (today video is only an unpriced add-on); neatlogs would supply the measured figure, per CLAUDE.md.

## 5. What is feasible before the deadline versus roadmap

Time: today is Sun 11 Oct; code freeze effectively Mon 12 Oct 19:00 IST when the submission window opens; the demo video is not made yet (HANDOFF) and must be at most 3:00.

**Feasible, smallest first (my time guesses, not measured):**
1. (1 to 2 h, no product change) A script that runs the cheap deterministic checks (`clip_present`, `clip_single_shot_calm`) and the two judge checks (`clip_hero_matches_drawing`, `clip_safe_visual`) on the clip we already have, logging to neatlogs and the ledger. It would show the oath catching hero drift with real numbers. Costs well under USD 0.05. This is the best evidence per hour.
2. (half a day) One optional "motion page" behind a flag: cover or page 1 only, Lite, 4 s, repair once, fallback to still, receipt line. Needs edits in `src/` (pipeline, config) which today already carry uncommitted changes; one intent per commit and a ledger run (B0 vs B1) are required by CLAUDE.md. Risk: Veo latency 11 s to 6 min eats the 240 s budget; run it in the background after the story is readable.
3. Rate and quota: unknown; one clip worked, a burst of retries may return 429 like images did.

**Roadmap (do not promise in the demo):**
- Hero reference images on Veo 3.1 Fast; per-child character sheet.
- Page-choosing agent with learned "motion value"; first/last-frame to join pages smoothly.
- Independent clip judge with calibration against a human-labelled set of clips (like `scripts/eval_judge.py` for text): injected faults such as extra limb, text on screen, flash, wrong hero.
- Open-weight route (Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B on a 24 GB GPU) for no data leaving our control; needs a GPU the AWS allowance probably cannot fund.
- Privacy review: a child's drawing goes to a video vendor. Vertex terms for Veo inputs and retention: **not verified**; Gemini API says generated videos are kept 2 days. Real children's drawings must stay out of this path until a parent consents and terms are read (CLAUDE.md rule 3).
- Safety review for ages 4 to 8 beyond frames: no jump scares, no sudden loud sounds (we mute Veo audio), no photorealistic faces, a stricter motion prompt, and a human spot check of the first 50 clips.

**Honest view.** Generative video is a risky fit for "my own drawing comes alive": identity drifts (seen on the first try), clips cost 4 to 20 times what a page picture costs, latency is long, and it adds a data vendor. The oath gives us the right answer to that risk, and the cheapest credible demo is step 1 above plus, if time allows, step 2 on one page. Deterministic motion stays the default.

# Video generation for Storybound: access, landscape, and a plan

Written Sun 11 Oct 2026 by a research pass. Only `docs/research/video-generation.md` and `evidence/video-gen/` were created; no `src/` or `web/` file was touched. No key appears here. "Not verified" means I could not check it; most web facts below come from secondary pages and are marked as such.

## 0. What we have access to (checked 11 Oct, about 10:30 IST)

| Route | Video or image-to-video? | How I checked | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vertex AI, project in `config.py`, `us-central1`, gcloud ADC | **Yes.** `veo-2.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.0-fast-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-fast-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-lite-generate-001` are listed | `genai.Client(vertexai=True).models.list()` (129 models) | Listed is not the same as quota. One real call with the Lite model worked (see 1) |
| Vertex AI, location `global` (what `config.py` uses today) | No Veo models listed (27 models) | same call | Video must use a regional endpoint, `us-central1` worked. Not tried: other regions |
| Hackathon LiteLLM gateway | **No.** 7 models: `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` | `GET /models` | No video model. Claude models could act as an independent vision judge for clip frames (image input through the gateway not tested) |
| K2 (`IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B`) | No, text only | `docs/PLATFORMS.md`; not re-listed today | Stays the text judge |
| AWS (hackathon account) | No | CLAUDE.md rule 5 | No Bedrock, so no Nova Reel or Luma on Bedrock |
| Quotas and billing | Not read | I did not open the Vertex quota page or billing console | Actual charge for the test clip: **not verified** |

## 1. The one-clip test (done)

- Model `veo-3.1-lite-generate-001`, `us-central1`, image-to-video from `assets/test-drawings/benign/bunny-bow-carrot.png` (a hackathon sample, not a real child's file), 4 s, 720p, 16:9, `generate_audio=False`, 1 video.
- Result: **success, 43.5 s wall time**, 1 video, 0 filtered by the safety layer. MP4 H.264 1280x720, 4.000 s, **no audio stream** (checked with ffprobe), 778 KB.
- Estimated cost: 4 s x USD 0.05/s = **USD 0.20**, using the Gemini API list price for Lite at 720p (see 2). The Vertex price and any no-audio discount are not verified.
- Files: `evidence/video-gen/bunny-veo31lite-4s.mp4`, `bunny-veo31lite-4s.json` (parameters, latency, estimate, no credentials) and `bunny-veo31lite-4s-frames-0-50-95.png` (frames at 0, 50, 95).
- What I saw by eye, which matters for the oath: colours, bow, carrot and magenta outline were kept, but the **face was redrawn** (lashes, pink cheeks, a new nose), **arms and a leg were added**, the **tail shrank**, and the 4:3 drawing was **pillarboxed** with black bars. The motion is calm and nothing scary. For a child who drew this bunny, "that is not my bunny" is the real risk, and it is exactly what a per-clip hero check should catch.

Not tested: reference images (Lite does not take them), first-and-last frame, clip extension, other Veo models, image-to-video of a drawing that contains a person (see 2, person rules).

## 2. Veo facts (Gemini API docs; Vertex equivalents not verified)

From https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/veo (fetched today):
- Veo 3.1 durations 4, 6, 8 s; 24 fps; 720p default, 1080p and 4k only at 8 s; Lite has no 4k.
- **Up to 3 reference images** for subject appearance, only on Veo 3.1 standard and Fast, **8 s required**; **Lite does not accept them**.
- First frame (`image`) plus optional `lastFrame`: Veo 3.1 models only.
- Extension: +7 s, up to 20 times, up to 148 s total; not on Lite; 720p only.
- Latency 11 s to 6 min at peak. Every video carries a SynthID watermark. Blocked videos are not charged.
- Image-to-video and reference images: `personGeneration` is `allow_adult` only. How a child's drawing of a child is treated: not tested.
- The page says audio is always generated; on Vertex `generate_audio=False` gave a silent file, so that page is not the whole story.

Prices, USD per second, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (Gemini API, paid tier, video with audio): Veo 3.1 standard 0.40 (720p and 1080p), 0.60 (4k); Fast 0.10 (720p), 0.12 (1080p), 0.30 (4k); **Lite 0.05 (720p), 0.08 (1080p)**. Launch coverage of Lite: https://the-decoder.com/googles-veo-3-1-lite-cuts-video-generation-costs-by-more-than-half/. Vertex's own price page would not render for me; a third-party page quotes a lower video-only tier on Vertex (Lite 0.03/0.05), **not verified**. Runway's official page hosts Veo 3.1 at half price without audio (see 3), a hint that a silent clip may be cheaper; also not verified for Vertex.

## 3. The landscape (what exists, how it keeps characters the same)

Legend: licence / consistency method / clip length / cost / fit for a 4 to 8 year old's own drawing. "nv" = not verified.

### Commercial video models
- **Google Veo 3.1 and Flow.** Veo above. Flow adds "Ingredients" (up to 3 reference images per prompt), "Scenebuilder" (arrange, trim, extend clips) and "Frames to Video" (start and end frame): https://nofilmschool.com/google-flow-ai-filmmaking-tool, https://blog.google/technology/ai/flow-video-tips/ (secondary description; Flow's own docs not read). Consistency: reference images, first/last frame, extend. Clips 4 to 8 s. Cost: see 2. Fit: best for us because we already run on Vertex and use ADC; the weak point is the first-frame-only mode (Lite) drifting, as seen in 1.
- **Runway** (API). Official docs https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing/ : 1 credit = USD 0.01; `gen4_turbo` 5 credits/s (0.05 USD/s), `gen4.5` 12 (0.12), hosted `veo3.1` 40 audio / 20 no audio, `veo3.1_fast` 15 / 10. Max clip length and reference-image features: nv. Fit: a second vendor, but adds a key, a data processor for children's drawings and a new billing line; not needed this weekend.
- **Kling** (Kuaishou). Third-party price snapshots only: Kling 3.0 image-to-video about 0.075 USD/s on a router, official about 0.10 to 0.16 USD/s: https://evolink.ai/blog/kling-3-api-pricing-integration-guide (secondary, sources disagree). Element/reference control is mentioned, how well it works: nv.
- **Luma Ray.** Sources conflict (per-clip 0.30 USD for 5 s at 720p, or about 0.24 USD/s at 1080p): https://wavespeed.ai/blog/cost-and-billing/luma-ai-pricing/. Official page not read.
- **Pika.** Not verified (search returned nothing usable).
- **OpenAI Sora.** Secondary sources say the consumer app ended 26 Apr 2026 and the API was due to end 24 Sep 2026; unconfirmed by OpenAI: https://www.cometapi.com/sora-api-access-in-2026-pricing-rate-limits-and-what-s-actually-available-through-aggregators/. Do not plan on it.

### Open-weight models (all need a GPU we do not have; AWS has EC2 only with a $25 team allowance)
- **Wan 2.2** (Alibaba). Apache 2.0 per the official repo (https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan2.2). I2V-A14B 480p/720p needs at least 80 GB of GPU memory; TI2V-5B does 720p at 24 fps, "5-second 720P in under 9 minutes" on one 24 GB card (RTX 4090). Clips about 5 s (secondary: https://wan27.org/blog/wan-2-2-longer-than-5-seconds). Consistency: image conditioning; character LoRA is the community's route. Fit: licence is clean; cost and ops are the problem on this account.
- **LTX-Video / LTX-2** (Lightricks). Community open-weights licence: free commercially under USD 10M annual revenue, group-wide, plus restrictions on substitute offerings (secondary summary of https://static.lightricks.com/legal/ltx-2-open-weights-license-0.X.pdf; read the text before use). Clip length and image-to-video limits: nv.
- **HunyuanVideo** (Tencent). Community licence that, per secondary sources, **excludes the EU, UK and South Korea** (https://deepwiki.com/Tencent/HunyuanVideo/5-license-and-legal). A product for families would have to geofence. Poor fit.
- **CogVideoX-5b-I2V** (Zhipu/THUDM). "CogVideoX LICENSE" (terms not read); 6 s, 8 fps, 720x480 only, 5 GB+ VRAM with offload: https://huggingface.co/THUDM/CogVideoX-5b-I2V. Low frame rate and size; fit weak.

### Research pipelines (story to video, multi-agent)
- **MovieAgent** (arXiv 2503.07314; https://github.com/showlab/MovieAgent). Director, screenwriter, storyboard and location-manager agents plan multi-scene films from a script and a "character bank". Model zoo lists SVD and HunyuanVideo-I2V; consistency through per-character ED-LoRA and ROICtrl. Licence not stated on the page. Heavy; needs LoRA training per character.
- **Anim-Director** (arXiv 2408.09787; code under HITsz-TMG). LMM agent writes script and character profiles, makes scene images with consistency prompts, then turns images into video. Licence nv.
- **VideoGen-of-Thought** (arXiv 2412.02259). Training-free: script, keyframes, shot video, smoothing; reports +20.4% face consistency and +17.4% style consistency over baselines (from the NeurIPS 2025 listing, https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/131787). Code and licence nv.
- **StoryAgent** (arXiv 2411.04925, ICLR 2025 per search). Story designer, storyboard and video agents; LoRA-BE image-to-video for shot consistency. Licence nv.
- **DreamFactory** (arXiv 2408.11788). Multi-agent, "key frames iteration" for cross-scene style and faces; introduces face-distance and style scores, which are the kind of measure our oath could reuse. Licence nv.
- **MAViS** (arXiv 2508.08487) and **MM-StoryAgent** (arXiv 2503.05242, narrated storybook video across text, image and audio): the latter is the closest in shape to Storybound. Licences nv.
- **ComfyUI.** Veo 3.1 and ElevenLabs are available as hosted "partner nodes" (secondary: https://comfyui.org/zh/elevenlabs-is-now-available-in-comfyui). "AI Movie Studio 2" (storyboard, reference-image continuity, timeline; https://comfyui-wiki.com/en/news/2026-09-09-ai-movie-studio-2) is young and its licence is nv.
- Common pattern in all of them: **write script, make keyframe images of the hero first, then animate each keyframe, then stitch.** None of them verifies the result against a promise; that is our gap to fill.

### Children's products (names from search results, none deeply checked)
- **Meta Animated Drawings**, MIT licence (code, weights, dataset) per https://github.com/facebookresearch/AnimatedDrawings. Rigs a human-shaped drawing and plays prerecorded motion. No generative drift, so a child's character cannot change; limited to humanoid figures, so a bunny may not fit. Not tested here.
- **KidsAI Art** (iPad app, sketch to picture or short video; https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784254113), **Storytime AI** (kids' books plus AI read-along videos; https://apps.apple.com/us/app/storytime-ai-story-generator/id6449826316), Kidslox "Kids Drawing Animator" (waitlist only). Licences, models and safety checks: nv. "Storytopia" exists as a Google competition entry for personalised stories without video (https://ai.google.dev/competition/projects/storytopia). I found no product that verifies each clip against stated promises; that is a claim about my search, not about the market.

### What a feature-length story needs (arithmetic, not a vendor claim)
Clips are 4 to 8 s. A 90-minute film is 5,400 s, so at least 700 to 1,350 clips. One pass at USD 0.05/s is USD 270; at USD 0.40/s it is USD 2,160, before retries (usually several per kept clip). The hard part is not cost but identity across hundreds of shots, which the projects above handle with reference images, key frames or per-character LoRA, and still need human selection. A 3-minute story is 180 s, USD 9 to 72 at those rates.

## 4. Recommended architecture for Storybound

### Principle
Video is an optional upgrade of a page that has **already passed** its image checks. The oath decides whether the child sees the clip; if any clip check fails, the child sees the verified still (plus the existing HyperFrames read-along motion). Nothing unverified is ever shown.

### Pipeline
1. `motion_planner` (agent, cheap text model): reads the verified 8 pages and the budget, picks which pages to animate and writes a motion prompt per page (below).
2. `animate` (tool): Veo image-to-video, **first frame = the verified page illustration** (it already matched the character card at 0.8); for the cover or page 1, the **child's own drawing** is the first frame for the "my drawing woke up" moment. Prompt template: one calm action, "keep the flat crayon style, no text, no new characters, single shot, no camera cuts, slow gentle motion". Lite for first attempts; Veo 3.1 Fast with up to 3 reference images (drawing, character card, the page still) only for the hero page, 8 s, if budget allows (not tested).
3. `clip_verify` (oath): see below.
4. Repair once (regenerate with the failed check named in the prompt), else fall back to the still. Every fallback is listed on the receipt, as budget degradations already are.
5. Assembly: put the passing clips into the existing read-along movie. Whether HyperFrames can embed an MP4 cleanly: not verified; plain `ffmpeg` concat of segments is the fallback (ffmpeg exists on this machine at `C:\ffmpeg`).

### Per-clip commitments (same shape as `docs/DESIGN.md` 3.2)
| Commitment | Verifier | Sampling | On failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_present` | ffprobe: decodes, length 4 s +/- 0.3, size, **no audio stream** (child audio stays our own narration) | 1.0 | retry once, then still |
| `clip_single_shot_calm` | deterministic frame differencing on every frame: one scene, no hard cut, no strobe (WCAG three-flashes-per-second rule), bounded motion energy | 1.0 | still |
| `clip_no_text` | OCR or vision pass on 4 to 6 sampled frames; any legible word fails (matches `no_drawing_text_obedience`) | 1.0 | regenerate once, then still |
| `clip_safe_visual` (core) | vision judge on the sampled frames with the real image bytes; fail closed on any error | **1.0, cannot be lowered** | still, critical detection |
| `clip_hero_present` | vision judge: the hero from the character card is visible in at least 3 of 4 frames | 1.0 (cheap) | regenerate once |
| `clip_hero_matches_drawing` | vision judge on first, middle and last frame against the **drawing** and the card's traits list (bow, carrot, colours, number of limbs); pass at 0.8 like `image_matches_card` | 1.0 for the test phase | regenerate once, then still; **the test clip in 1 would likely have failed this** |
| `clip_matches_page` | judge: the action in the page text is visible | 0.5 | regenerate once, then still |

Judge choice: the writer, the pictures and Veo are all Google, so the clip judge should be a different family. K2 is text only, so use `claude-sonnet-4.6` through the LiteLLM gateway for sampled frames (image input via the gateway **not tested**), keep `gemini-3.7-flash` as the cheap first-pass screen. Each judge call is one neatlogs GUARDRAIL span, so the clip story looks like the page story in the trace.

### Keeping the hero the child's
- Anchor on pixels: first frame is the drawing or the verified page, never text alone.
- Use traits from the character card as a checklist and count them before and after (our own test: eyes, nose, limbs and tail changed).
- Prefer short clips (4 s); drift grows with length and with extension chaining (community reports say quality degrades on continuation; secondary).
- Reference images (up to 3, 8 s) are the vendor's tool for identity; they need Veo 3.1 or Fast, so about USD 0.80 to 3.20 per 8 s clip at the listed rates. Not tested.
- If a drawing must never change, use deterministic motion (HyperFrames/GSAP bounce, sway, blink overlays, or Animated Drawings for human shapes). This is the zero-drift option and is what we ship today.

### Choosing pages within a budget
The agent receives `budget_usd` and `deadline_s` (the governor already exists in `config.py`: USD 1.5 and 240 s per story). Rule: the base story costs about USD 0.44 (HANDOFF: about 0.40 plus 0.04 movie), so about USD 1.0 is left. Score pages by (a) an action verb the hero performs, (b) the page where the lesson's correct choice is revealed, (c) the cover, (d) the page's image already passed at a high margin (a safe first frame). Pick the top N such that estimated cost x 1.4 (retry allowance) fits; **degrade order**: drop clips before dropping any safety check, as DESIGN.md already says for judges. Show the choice and cost on the receipt.

### Cost per story (estimates, Gemini API list prices, Vertex not verified)
| Plan | Clips | Veo cost | With 1.4 retry allowance | Plus base 0.44 and clip judges (about 0.05, my guess) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 1 | 0.20 | 0.28 | about 0.77 |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 3 | 0.60 | 0.84 | about 1.33 (inside the 1.5 budget) |
| Lite 720p, 4 s | 8 (all pages) | 1.60 | 2.24 | about 2.7 (over budget) |
| Fast 720p, 4 s | 3 | 1.20 | 1.68 | about 2.2 (over budget) |
| Fast 720p, 8 s with references, hero page only | 1 | 0.80 | 1.12 | about 1.6 (slightly over) |

So the budget supports **one to three Lite clips per story**. The cfo.ai model would need a "motion add-on" line (today video is only an unpriced add-on); neatlogs would supply the measured figure, per CLAUDE.md.

## 5. What is feasible before the deadline versus roadmap

Time: today is Sun 11 Oct; code freeze effectively Mon 12 Oct 19:00 IST when the submission window opens; the demo video is not made yet (HANDOFF) and must be at most 3:00.

**Feasible, smallest first (my time guesses, not measured):**
1. (1 to 2 h, no product change) A script that runs the cheap deterministic checks (`clip_present`, `clip_single_shot_calm`) and the two judge checks (`clip_hero_matches_drawing`, `clip_safe_visual`) on the clip we already have, logging to neatlogs and the ledger. It would show the oath catching hero drift with real numbers. Costs well under USD 0.05. This is the best evidence per hour.
2. (half a day) One optional "motion page" behind a flag: cover or page 1 only, Lite, 4 s, repair once, fallback to still, receipt line. Needs edits in `src/` (pipeline, config) which today already carry uncommitted changes; one intent per commit and a ledger run (B0 vs B1) are required by CLAUDE.md. Risk: Veo latency 11 s to 6 min eats the 240 s budget; run it in the background after the story is readable.
3. Rate and quota: unknown; one clip worked, a burst of retries may return 429 like images did.

**Roadmap (do not promise in the demo):**
- Hero reference images on Veo 3.1 Fast; per-child character sheet.
- Page-choosing agent with learned "motion value"; first/last-frame to join pages smoothly.
- Independent clip judge with calibration against a human-labelled set of clips (like `scripts/eval_judge.py` for text): injected faults such as extra limb, text on screen, flash, wrong hero.
- Open-weight route (Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B on a 24 GB GPU) for no data leaving our control; needs a GPU the AWS allowance probably cannot fund.
- Privacy review: a child's drawing goes to a video vendor. Vertex terms for Veo inputs and retention: **not verified**; Gemini API says generated videos are kept 2 days. Real children's drawings must stay out of this path until a parent consents and terms are read (CLAUDE.md rule 3).
- Safety review for ages 4 to 8 beyond frames: no jump scares, no sudden loud sounds (we mute Veo audio), no photorealistic faces, a stricter motion prompt, and a human spot check of the first 50 clips.

**Honest view.** Generative video is a risky fit for "my own drawing comes alive": identity drifts (seen on the first try), clips cost 4 to 20 times what a page picture costs, latency is long, and it adds a data vendor. The oath gives us the right answer to that risk, and the cheapest credible demo is step 1 above plus, if time allows, step 2 on one page. Deterministic motion stays the default.

They keep characters consistent via per-character LoRA, key frames and reference images. I found no product that verifies each clip against stated promises (a claim about my search only).
7. Recommended architecture: animate only pages that already passed their image checks, using the verified page still (or the child's drawing for the cover) as the first frame. Seven per-clip oath checks: present, single-shot and calm (frame differencing), no text, safe (judge, sampling 1.0), hero present, hero matches the drawing (pass at 0.8), and matches the page text. Claude Sonnet via the gateway is the suggested independent frame judge (image input untested). On a failed check, regenerate once, then fall back to the verified still plus today's HyperFrames motion.
8. Cost per story (estimates): with the 1.4 retry allowance and about $0.44 base, 1 Lite clip is about $0.77 and 3 Lite clips about $1.33, inside the $1.5 budget. All 8 pages on Lite is about $2.7 and 3 Fast clips about $2.2, both over budget. Feature-length is arithmetic only: about 675 to 1,350 clips, $270 to $2,160 for one pass at $0.05 to $0.40/s.
9. Feasible before Mon 19:00 IST: (a) a 1 to 2 hour script that runs the clip checks on the existing clip, to show the oath catching hero drift, for under $0.05; (b) an optional flagged one-page motion feature in half a day, which needs edits in src/. These are my time guesses, not measured. Roadmap: Veo reference images, a calibrated clip judge, an open-weight GPU route, a privacy review of sending drawings to Veo (not verified), and a stricter safety review.
10. Honest view: generative video is a risky fit for "my own drawing comes alive" because identity drifts, it costs 4 to 20 times a page picture, and it is slow. Deterministic motion should stay the default, with video as an oath-gated extra.
